# Update an installed AI-Forward Pack

Use this skill when a repository already has AI-Forward and you want to refresh it to a newer local pack revision without hand-copying files or losing local deviations.

## When to use it

Use `updatepack` in the repository that already has the pack installed. It is for maintenance of the pack surface, not for changing product code. For a first install, use [addpacktorepo](#skill-addpacktorepo).

## What you need

You need a local AI-Forward source clone and the target repository's installed `docs/ai-forward-pack/INSTALL.md`. If the update reports conflicts or review rows, a human must decide how local changes survive.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/updatepack C:\Projects\ai-forward --dry-run
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$updatepack C:\Projects\ai-forward --dry-run
```

Run without `--dry-run` after reviewing the table.

## What happens

The skill reads the source and installed revisions, then runs the source pack's update program against the target. It repastes managed blocks, removes stale installed copies, advances the installed revision, and reports conflicts instead of hiding them.

## What you get

Illustrative output shape:

```text
Pack updated: revision 82 -> 84
Action     Path                                      Meaning
UPDATE     .github/prompts/specify.prompt.md         source changed
MERGE      AGENTS.md                                 local text carried forward
REMOVE     .github/instructions/old.instructions.md  stale installed copy
CONFLICT   .claude/skills/example/SKILL.md           needs human resolution
```

The skill offers a commit after checks pass.

## Review before continuing

Do not accept “done” while conflicts remain, `docs/docs-index.js` changed, duplicate managed blocks exist, or retained local text has nowhere to live. Read warnings from the doctor script; some are user-level choices, but they must be understood.

## Tips and recovery

Always preview large jumps. If a script path in documentation says `python3` on Windows, use `python` or `py -3`. If the update changes coordination or hooks, requalify the harness behavior before relying on it.

## Where to go next

Use [auditlog](#skill-auditlog) to see when the pack was last refreshed, or [session-profiler](#skill-session-profiler) if the update was meant to fix session drift.
